subject: houndeye
label: houndeye, in the place of the game's models/houndeye.mdl

measured.lineup: ours is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/barney.mdl, models/hassassin.mdl, models/scientist.mdl: the judge does not know which

M1.reason: The body is a round, slightly squat yellow ball with one red eye on the front, which matches the brief. The outline fails on the legs: the front, left and back views show four or more tube legs, plus stubs, where the brief asks for three thin legs. The extra legs stick out in every side view.

M2.reason: Measured size is 53.1 x 44.6 x 46.5. Height is 44.6 against 45 asked (about 1% off) and length 53.1 against 49 asked (about 8% off). Both are within 15%, and the measured sizeOff of 0.083 agrees.

M3.reason: Parts the brief asks for, down to the small ones: three thin legs, one large eye on the front, striped and dappled hide, and no claws, teeth, rivets or handles. The eye is present on the front (front and front-left views). The leg count is wrong: the front, left, back-right and back-left views show four legs plus extra stubs, not three. A wrong count of a main component caps M3 at 1.

M4.reason: The body is an even yellow, as the brief says, with a dark red eye and dark brown stripes. The colours sit within one family across the regions, and nothing is out of place in the side or top views.

M5.reason: Striped: dark slashes on the top in the top, front and side views. Dappled: dark spots on the top and at the side of the body, and a mottled texture across the hide. Both read at a close look. The stripes are on the top more than the flanks, which the brief does not fix.

M6.reason: In the line-up the asset is B, and it reads at once as a crude prop: a bulb body with tube legs and a flat red blob for an eye. Next to the game's humanoids a player would not take it for a Half-Life model. The line-up is not of its own kind, so this is a judgement of the asset's build, not a like-for-like match.

M7.reason: The eye faces the front, the body is upright, and the legs hold the body up in the front and side views. The front is the brief's front.

M8.reason: The SMAK check reports no errors. At 472 triangles it is well under twice the median of Half-Life's props of its kind (1152) and under three quarters of them (740). Nothing is reported as open or floating.

C1.reason: The run (motion.png, frames 0 to 36) keeps the body and legs together, with no part sinking through the floor. The legs look loose at their joints in several frames (frames 15 and 36 show a stub at the top right that does not clearly join the body). The brief's charge with a sonic blast is not shown, so the attack half is not judged.
